parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define electric potential at a point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A hydrogen atom may be considered to consist of a proton and an electron separated by a distance of 120 pm, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The two particles may be considered as point charges.

Point P lies on the line joining the electron and the proton and is at a variable distance *x* from the proton.
parts.text: Show that the electric potential *V* at point P when *x* = 10 pm is equal to 130 V.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate, to two significant figures, *V* when *x* = 30 pm.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: On Fig. 5.1, draw a cross (×) at one position, other than infinity, where the electric potential is zero.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
On Fig. 5.2, sketch the variation of *V* with *x* between *x* = 10 pm and *x* = 110 pm.

[[fig:f2]]

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: A proton and an electron are shown 120 pm apart, with point P between them at a distance x from the proton.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.2
figures.alt: A blank grid for sketching electric potential V against distance x, with axes labelled V / V and x / pm, spanning x = 10 to 110 pm and V = −160 to 160 V.
